## Gotchas

Homepage and archive selections follow the shared JSON order. Featured projects
use the first case-study figure as their cover when present; other entries use
the screenshot map in src/lib/project-visuals.ts. Keep either image source
available when changing the selected work.

Newsreader is loaded with `weight: "variable"`; next/font refuses `axes` with a
fixed weight list.

Do not run `vercel --prod`. It does not move the production alias.

Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights are installed in the layout. Analytics
is enabled and collecting; Speed Insights needs real visits before its dashboard
has enough measurements. Their scripts are served by Vercel, so a plain local
production preview returns 404 for those two paths.

`npm run check-links` proves a URL answers, not that the site is ours.
shipyard.vercel.app returned 200 for two months while belonging to someone
else. Take a project's URL from its own repo or its Vercel project, never from
the `<name>.vercel.app` pattern.

## Interface fixes — November 22

Prepared on `claude/lucid-ritchie-t6aqp0` from master `25f1162`. The user asked for the recommended interface fixes and accepted a light-only site.

## Audit fixes — November 25

Prepared on `claude/lucid-ritchie-t6aqp0` from master `f799639`. A read-only audit of the live site found no broken page and no accessibility violation (Lighthouse on a simulated phone: performance 90 to 97, accessibility, best practices and search 100). The user asked for its five fixes and for the recommended answer to the résumé question.

- Next.js and `eslint-config-next` move from 16.3.8 to 16.4.6. `npm audit` listed a group of advisories rated critical for 16.0.0 to 16.4.4. The site uses no server actions, no `use cache` and no middleware, so most of them do not apply, but the image-optimizer ones could not be ruled out. `npm audit fix` also cleared the development-only `minimatch` and `zod` advisories. `npm audit` now reports nothing.
- Reachspan: the "Live site" link goes to the English page, `https://www.reachspan.ai/en.html`. The bare domain opens in Chinese, while the portfolio shows the English screenshot. The description, the home summary and the carousel summary now say the site is for Hong Kong businesses and is in Chinese and English.
- Reachspan project notes gain one line about ViralSignal: since September 2026, AI coding agents were directed to audit and rework that app, and the résumé describes the work. The résumé leads with ViralSignal and the site did not mention it, so a reader going from one to the other found nothing. ViralSignal still has no page of its own and stays `resumeOnly`; the line repeats the résumé's wording and claims nothing more.

- Four security headers are sent with every response (see `docs/STACK.md`). HSTS already came from the host.
- Removed leftovers: `CHECKPOINT.md`, `design-qa.md`, `docs/traffic/SEO-CHECKPOINT.md`, the `qa/` folder and the unused duplicate `public/projects/reachspan.png`. `LINKS_CHECKED_ON` is gone from `src/lib/site.ts`: no page had shown the date since the redesign, and it still read 2026-09-03. `npm run check-links` now only checks and reports; it changes no file.

Not done: two page descriptions are still cut mid-sentence (Amex Roofing, How's My Job Fit?), three case-study titles are over 60 characters, and the sitemap dates of unchanged pages are old. The site gets few visitors and almost none from search, so these were left.

## Home heading drawn as ink — November 26, preview only

Prepared on `claude/lucid-ritchie-t6aqp0` from master `3e98d98`. **Nothing here is merged.** The branch is pushed so that Vercel builds a preview for the user to try.

- Background: the user asked for a plan for a 3D interactive portfolio. A 3D "work table" page (three.js and a physics engine) was built on this branch and then withdrawn at the user's request. It is reverted in `1785b7a` and `b46b700`; the code remains in the history from `97e1b59` and `f9b07d7`. The user then chose a different direction: no 3D scene, but WebGL effects on the existing pages.
- This change is the first of those effects. `src/components/HeroInk.tsx` draws the home page name on a canvas over the `h1`. At rest it matches the text (115 of 639,200 pixels differ noticeably in a screenshot comparison). Moving the pointer across it, or scrolling on a phone, carries the letters like wet ink, shows the home page's yellow under them, and lets them flow back. One light stroke runs across the name when the page has loaded.
- It uses WebGL 2 directly: no new dependency, about 4 KB of script. `docs/STACK.md` describes how it works and when it stays off (software rendering, reduced motion, no WebGL 2, no JavaScript).
- Checked in a headless browser with a simulated graphics card: it starts on desktop and phone sizes, logs nothing to the console, causes no horizontal overflow, and returns to the exact resting picture. It stays off on software rendering and with reduced motion. Lighthouse on the home page is unchanged (performance 91, accessibility 100, no layout shift).
- Not checked, because it needs a real device: how the movement feels and how smooth it is. That is the user's call from the preview.
- Possible next effects in the same direction, not started: transitions between the project pictures in the home carousel, and short recordings of the products in place of still screenshots (the recordings would have to come from the user).
